title: A Noetherian reduced separated scheme of dimension at most one has an ample invertible module
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] which is Noetherian (locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] and quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]), reduced [def-pc-reduced-scheme] and separated (the structure morphism $X\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ is separated [def-weil-proper-morphism]), and whose underlying topological space has Krull dimension $\dim X\le1$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension] ($X=\varnothing$ allowed). Then there exists an invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal L$ [def-sc-invertible-module] which is ample [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module].

source.place: Varieties, Lemma 09NX (varieties-lemma-dim-1-noetherian-reduced-separated-has-ample, line 8080), stated there for dimension 1; its proof uses Lemma 09ND (varieties-lemma-dim-1-noetherian-integral-separated-has-ample, line 7927), Lemma 09NE (varieties-lemma-glue-invertible-sheaves), Remark 09NW (varieties-remark-conductor), Properties Lemma 09NV (properties-lemma-ample-finite-set-in-principal-affine), Limits Lemma 09NL (limits-lemma-affines-glued-in-closed-affine), Properties Proposition 01Q3 (properties-proposition-characterize-ample) and Properties Lemma 01PV (properties-lemma-affine-cap-s-open); the case dim X <= 1 is the one Lemma 0A25 needs

proof.text: If $X=\varnothing$ or $\dim X\le0$, [lem-sc-zero-dim-noetherian-affine] makes $X$ affine and $\mathcal O_X$ ample. This includes finite discrete unions of reduced closed points and the empty scheme. Henceforth assume $\dim X=1$.

source.place: Properties Lemmas 0AAX and 0CKV; dimension-zero branch omitted from the statement of Varieties Lemma 09NX

proof.text: Let $Z_1,\ldots,Z_r$ be the finitely many irreducible components of $X$, each with its reduced closed subscheme structure. Each $Z_i$ is integral, Noetherian and separated as a closed subscheme of $X$, and has dimension $0$ or $1$. By [lem-sc-integral-dim-one-ample] in dimension $1$ and [lem-sc-zero-dim-noetherian-affine] in dimension $0$, choose an ample invertible $\mathcal O_{Z_i}$-module $\mathcal L_i$. The set $T=\bigcup_{i\ne j}(Z_i\cap Z_j)$ is a finite set of closed points, and each $x\notin T$ lies on exactly one component, by [lem-sc-component-intersections-finite].

source.place: Varieties Lemma 09NX, proof, first three sentences; Lemma 09ND; Properties Lemma 0CKV for zero-dimensional components

proof.text: For each $i$, apply [lem-sc-ample-finite-principal-affine] to $E=T\cap Z_i$, $W=Z_i$ and $\mathcal L_i$. Replace $\mathcal L_i$ by the resulting positive power and obtain $s_i$ whose affine nonvanishing locus $(Z_i)_{s_i}$ contains $T\cap Z_i$. The intersections $Z_i\cap Z_j$ are finite discrete spaces (step 2); therefore [lem-sc-glue-component-line-bundles] gives an invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal L$ and a section $s$ restricting to each $s_i$.

source.place: Varieties Lemma 09NX, proof, first and second paragraphs; Properties Lemma 09NV; Varieties Lemma 09NE

proof.text: The open $X_s$ contains $T$. Its closed subschemes $(Z_i)_{s_i}$ are affine and their underlying sets cover $X_s$; as $Z_i$ is closed in $X$, each is closed in $X_s$. Apply [lem-sc-closed-affine-union-affine] to conclude that $X_s$ is affine.

source.place: Varieties Lemma 09NX, proof, second paragraph; Limits Lemma 09NL

proof.text: Fix $x\in X\setminus T$, lying on the unique component $Z_1$ (step 2). Let $Z$ be the reduced union of the other components, with ideal $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_X$, and let $\mathcal I_1$ be its image in $\mathcal O_{Z_1}$. Then $x\notin V(\mathcal I_1)$: otherwise $x$ would lie on both $Z_1$ and $Z$. Applying [lem-sc-ample-ideal-section] to the ample $\mathcal L_1$ and ideal $\mathcal I_1$ gives $m_1>0$ and $t_1\in\Gamma(Z_1,\mathcal I_1\mathcal L_1^{\otimes m_1})$ nonvanishing at $x$. The definition of ampleness [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module] gives $m_2>0$ and $t_2\in\Gamma(Z_1,\mathcal L_1^{\otimes m_2})$ with $x\in(Z_1)_{t_2}$ affine.

source.place: Varieties Lemma 09NX, proof, final paragraph; Properties Proposition 01Q3 and Definition 01PS

proof.text: Set $m=m_1+m_2$ and $t=t_1t_2$. Multiplication places $t$ in $\Gamma(Z_1,\mathcal I_1\mathcal L_1^{\otimes m})$, and its nonvanishing locus is $(Z_1)_t=(Z_1)_{t_1}\cap(Z_1)_{t_2}$, containing $x$. It is affine by [lem-sc-affine-cap-section-open] applied to the affine open $(Z_1)_{t_2}$ and the section $t_1$.

source.place: Varieties Lemma 09NX, proof, final four sentences; Properties Lemma 01PV

proof.text: By [lem-sc-conductor-sections], $t$ extends to a global section $\widetilde t$ of $\mathcal L^{\otimes m}$ vanishing on all components except $Z_1$. Its nonvanishing locus $X_{\widetilde t}$ equals $(Z_1)_t$, which is affine and contains $x$ by step 6. Together with the affine $X_s$ for points of $T$ (step 4), these sections verify the defining criterion [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module] at every point of the quasi-compact Noetherian scheme $X$. Thus $\mathcal L$ is ample.

source.place: Varieties Lemma 09NX, proof, conductor equality and conclusion; Varieties Remark 09NW

proof_origin.place: Varieties Lemma 09NX (varieties-lemma-dim-1-noetherian-reduced-separated-has-ample), with dimension-zero branch from Properties Lemmas 0AAX and 0CKV
